retrieved_evidence.text_excerpt: **The Mireward Reach** is the drove-road and wheel-way that carries trade, troops, and rumor north from Mirathorn toward the fen country and the swamp frontier — past Outtown, waystations, and towns like Mossford that earn their living from distance. It is not one king’s highway; it is a braid of maintained crown span, patched county line, and mud tracks honest cartwrights swear by.

**Table canon (Session 21):** **Mireward** is the **next little town north** on the Mireward Reach — about **five days** from the party’s conical-hill camp at end Session 21 (~five days from Mirathorn along the same road).

*Mireward is a pension town with a bell tower and a ferry — retired spears, stink-trades, and people who wanted sky instead of spires. The wall still stands; the patrols still ride; it’s just that the festival has the young guards in Mirathorn singing, one long patrol is still out on the fen rotation, and nobody alive remembers the last time the weird north really came for them. The road economy still looks fine from the apron. The haylofts tell a different story.*

| | | |--|--| | **Work** | **Fuller’s Row**, second-generation; hands permanently stained; knows every refugee by **smell of their laundry**. | | **Politics** | **Annual mock reeve campaign** (“Merrow Ironveil — Reeve of Honest Air”) — one speech, one banner, zero votes, **maximum embarrassment**. | | **Toward Lysandra** | Fierce pride **weaponized as criticism**: *“Don’t you dare salute me, I’m your **mother**.”* Will **corner her in downwind lane** if party enters town. | | **Toward Mirathorn** | *“Spire noise.”* Blames **Commander Thalia** for “stealing her sensible child.” |

- *“Road’s open. Town’s full. I’m not opening for wagons till dawn unless you’re bleeding or useful — and my **daughter** doesn’t count as useful till she says hello to her **father**.”* - *“Write **foot only** — and if the axle folk want a miracle they can lift like the hymn says.”* - On rank: *“You look like you’ve been **eating rank** again.”*

- Storm fronts made the first march day tense; we need to plan the next weather roll beat for Session 23. - Hester Mull appeared as a courier encounter; unresolved whether the party trusts the detour offer.

retrieved_evidence.text_excerpt: They continue on north with Karsemine and Caelynn keeping an eye out for high ground for a place to stop for the night. While on this short trip everyone is able to relax and have a short rest. Because of their timing leaving the town and their navigation skills, the wagon is able to make it far enough north to just hit the very edge of the storm and only get soaked. They are able to see the sheen of magic as the rain pools up and instead of the usual petrichor the rain smells savory. Karsemine and Caelynn spot a good camping spot on the top of a conical hill. They leave the wagon and the animals at the bottom and make their way up until they reach a giant bowl of water surrounded by a grove
